questions.q: How are the three nested containers in Excel ordered?
options: A workbook holds worksheets, and each worksheet is a grid of cells
questions.explain: The workbook is the file, worksheets are tabs, and cells are addressed by column letter and row number.

questions.q: What does the Name Box let you do besides showing the selected address?
options: Type an address such as B3 and press Enter to jump to it
questions.explain: It's the box above column A.

questions.q: What does A1:C5 represent?
options: A block 3 columns wide by 5 rows tall
questions.explain: A range is written TopLeft:BottomRight.

questions.q: What does Ctrl/Cmd+Arrow do?
options: Jumps to the edge of the current block of data in that direction
questions.explain: Adding Shift also extends the selection.

questions.q: What does every formula start with?
questions.explain: Every formula is = followed by an expression.

questions.q: You fill D2 (=C2-B2) down to D3. What does D3 contain?
questions.explain: Relative references shift as you copy them.

questions.q: What does the Formula Bar show for a cell with a formula?
options: The formula, while the cell shows the calculated result
questions.explain: The stored formula versus displayed value distinction matters constantly.

questions.q: What does =SUM(B2:B4,B6) do?
options: Sums four of the five rows, skipping B5
questions.explain: SUM accepts multiple ranges or cells, comma-separated.

questions.q: When you format 1200 as currency, what changes?
options: Only how it displays; the stored value is still 1200
questions.explain: Every formula referencing it still uses 1200.

questions.q: What does conditional formatting do?
options: Changes a cell's appearance automatically based on its value
questions.explain: It makes a budget's problem rows visually obvious.

questions.q: What happens to a cell's precision when you use Decrease Decimal?
options: Only the display is rounded; formulas use the full stored precision
questions.explain: Display rounding doesn't change the underlying value.

questions.q: What does the custom format $#,##0;[Red]-$#,##0 do?
options: Shows positives normally and negatives in red with a minus
questions.explain: It's a Custom format from More Number Formats.

questions.q: What does Insert > Table (Ctrl/Cmd+T) give you over a plain range?
options: Filtering, banded rows, auto-filling formulas and structured references
questions.explain: It turns the range into a structured object.

questions.q: What does =SUM(Budget[Actual]) have over =SUM(C2:C6)?
options: It adjusts automatically when rows are added or removed
questions.explain: A fixed range would need manual editing.

questions.q: What does Budget[@Actual] refer to?
options: The Actual value in that specific row
questions.explain: It is the structured-reference equivalent of a relative reference.

questions.q: Which table name is valid?
questions.explain: Table names must be unique, contain no spaces and can't collide with cell addresses.

questions.q: Which chart type does the lesson insert first for Budgeted vs Actual per category?
questions.explain: It shows one cluster of two bars (Budgeted, Actual) per category.

questions.q: What do the three floating buttons on a selected chart control?
options: Chart Elements, Chart Styles and Chart Filters
questions.explain: They cover most day-to-day chart adjustments without a separate dialog.

questions.q: Why might you uncheck Gridlines once Data Labels are showing?
options: Gridlines add visual noise when exact numbers are already displayed
questions.explain: Gridlines help estimate values only when labels are absent.

questions.q: How do you select non-adjacent columns such as Category and Budgeted for a pie chart?
options: Select A1:A7, then hold Ctrl/Cmd and select B1:B7
questions.explain: Ctrl/Cmd-click adds another range to the selection.

questions.q: In =VLOOKUP(A2,CategoryInfo!$A$2:$C$7,2,FALSE), what does 2 mean?
options: The 2nd column of the table array
questions.explain: The column index number is a fixed position, not a column name.

questions.q: What does FALSE as the last VLOOKUP argument request?
questions.explain: It is what you want almost always when matching text.

questions.q: What is VLOOKUP's biggest limitation?
options: It can only look rightward from the lookup column
It only works on one sheet
questions.explain: It also breaks if a column is inserted in the middle of the table array.

questions.q: How does XLOOKUP take its range arguments?
options: A lookup array and a separate return array
One table array and an index number
questions.explain: Its arguments are lookup value, lookup array and return array.

questions.q: What are IF's three arguments?
options: A condition, the value if TRUE and the value if FALSE
A cell, a row and a column
A range, a count and a sum
questions.explain: =IF(D2>0,"Over Budget","OK") shows the pattern.

questions.q: Rent's Difference is 0. What does =IF(D2>0,"Over Budget","OK") show?
questions.explain: 0>0 is FALSE.

questions.q: How does IFS differ from nested IFs?
options: It takes condition/result pairs and returns the first TRUE result, without nesting parentheses
questions.explain: Using TRUE as the final condition acts as a catch-all else.

questions.q: Why nest a second IF in the FALSE branch?
options: To get three outcomes (Over, Under, On Track) from one formula
questions.explain: A single IF only branches two ways.

questions.q: What kind of source data does a PivotTable need?
options: Flat, transaction-level data with one row per fact
questions.explain: The Transactions table has one row per category per month.

questions.q: What does converting the source to a Table give a PivotTable?
options: It auto-expands its source range when rows are added
questions.explain: PivotTables built from a Table pick up new rows.

questions.q: Dragging Category to Rows and Amount to Values defaults to what?
questions.explain: Rent totals 2400 across Jan and Feb.

questions.q: After swapping Category for Type in Rows, how many data rows appear?
questions.explain: Fixed = Rent 2400 + Savings 600 + Subscriptions 50.

questions.q: How do you restrict a cell to a dropdown of allowed values?
options: Data > Data Validation, Allow: List, with a Source range
questions.explain: The lesson uses =CategoryInfo!$A$2:$A$7 as the source.

questions.q: What is the difference between Stop and Warning error alert styles?
options: Stop blocks invalid entries; Warning lets the user override after confirming
questions.explain: Warning is useful when a value is unusual but not necessarily wrong.

questions.q: What does TRIM do?
options: Removes leading and trailing spaces and collapses internal multiple spaces to single spaces
questions.explain: It's the first step in cleaning pasted or imported text.

questions.q: Does Clear All in the Data Validation dialog change existing cell values?
options: No, it removes only the rule
questions.explain: The existing values stay as they were.

questions.q: Which formula pattern should the Difference column use?
options: =C2-B2 with relative references, not hardcoded values
questions.explain: Relative references fill down correctly.

questions.q: Why does the % of Budget column use an absolute reference to the Budgeted total?
options: So it doesn't break when copied
questions.explain: For example $B$8 or the Table's total row.

questions.q: What does the Needs Review column use?
questions.explain: It flags variable categories that are more than 50 over budget.

questions.q: Which four sheets make up the finished workbook?
questions.explain: Messy is the cleaning scratch sheet and can be deleted later.

questions.q: Where does the sum range go in SUMIFS compared with SUMIF?
options: First in SUMIFS, last in SUMIF
questions.explain: The lesson notes this trips up almost everyone coming from SUMIF.

questions.q: Using the Sales data, what does =SUMIFS(D2:D11,A2:A11,"East",B2:B11,"Mar") return?
questions.explain: Rows 4 (1500) and 8 (700) match East + Mar.

questions.q: =COUNTIFS(A2:A11,"West",D2:D11,">1000") returns 1. Why isn't the 1000 row counted?
questions.explain: Only row 7 (1300) qualifies.

questions.q: What does =AVERAGEIFS(D2:D11,C2:C11,"Priya") return?
questions.explain: Priya's deals 1500, 800, 600, 1000 sum to 3900 over 4 rows.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend to catch a mis-selected data range?
options: Cross-check the PivotTable totals against hand-calculated totals
questions.explain: East 4900 and West 5150 matched the hand sums.

questions.q: How do you get an average alongside the sum?
options: Drag Amount to Values a second time and change its Value Field Settings to Average
questions.explain: East's average is 4900/5 = 980.

questions.q: What controls nesting when you drag Month below Region in Rows?
options: The order of fields in the Rows box
questions.explain: Order matters: Region then Month nests months under each region.

questions.q: What does a calculated field Bonus = Amount*0.1 show for East's 4900?
Why use a secondary axis for Margin% alongside Revenue?
options: The scales differ by an order of magnitude, so the line would look flat on one axis
Secondary axes are required for all line charts
questions.explain: Revenue runs in thousands while Margin% is a fraction near 0.30.

questions.q: What is a sparkline?
options: A small in-cell trend line summarizing a column of values
questions.explain: One sparkline per KPI, stacked, gives a quick visual scan in dashboard headers.

questions.q: Which month has the lowest Revenue but the highest Margin% in the dataset?
questions.explain: March: 11000 revenue and 0.35 margin.

questions.q: How do you snap chart edges to cell boundaries when dragging?
questions.explain: This is the grid alignment principle for dashboard tiles.

questions.q: What does =INDIRECT(G1) do in the cascading dropdown?
options: Turns the text in G1 (e.g. "Fruit") into a reference to the named range of that name
questions.explain: G2's list changes to the items for whichever category G1 holds.

questions.q: What does the custom validation =AND(H2>0,H2<=100) allow?
options: Numbers above 0 up to and including 100
questions.explain: 150 and 0 are rejected; 100 is accepted.

questions.q: How does =COUNTIF($I$2:$I$10,I2)=1 block duplicates?
options: If the value already appears, the count becomes 2, returning FALSE and rejecting it
questions.explain: Only a first occurrence gives a count of 1.

questions.q: What do Form Controls like combo boxes and check boxes let a sheet do?
options: Respond to user clicks without VBA
questions.explain: First enable the Developer tab in Customize Ribbon.

questions.q: What makes Power Query repeatable?
options: Every action is recorded as a numbered Applied Step that replays on refresh
questions.explain: Manual copy/paste cleanup would have to be redone each time.

questions.q: Why Replace Values (null → 0) rather than Fill Down for a blank sales cell?
options: A missing figure should become 0, not inherit a neighbor's value
questions.explain: Row 5 becomes Alan, EAST, 0.

questions.q: After cleaning, what does Group By region with Sum of sales show?
Why normalize region case to one convention?
options: So East and east aren't treated as separate groups downstream
questions.explain: Pick one convention and apply it everywhere.

questions.q: What does 'spill' mean for dynamic array functions?
options: Results automatically fill neighboring cells, with no Ctrl+Shift+Enter needed
questions.explain: FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE and SEQUENCE return multiple results.

questions.q: How do you combine two conditions inside FILTER as AND?
questions.explain: Multiplication acts as AND and returns 3 rows in the example.

questions.q: What does =SORT(UNIQUE(B2:B9)) return for the Team data?
questions.explain: UNIQUE gives first-seen order Sales, IT, HR; SORT orders it alphabetically.

questions.q: What does the # operator in I1# refer to?
questions.explain: =COUNTIF(B2:B9,I1#) spills counts aligned to the sorted departments.

questions.q: What does Goal Seek do in the loan model?
options: Iterates to find the input (e.g. Principal) that produces a target output (e.g. a 350 payment)
questions.explain: It solves for B1 so that B4 reaches 350, roughly 18122.

questions.q: In a one-variable Data Table with rates listed down a column, which input cell do you specify?
questions.explain: Rates vary down a column, so B2 is the column input cell.

questions.q: What sanity check does the lesson give for the Data Table results?
options: Payments rise monotonically as the rate increases from 0.04 to 0.08
questions.explain: At 0.08 expect roughly 405.53, higher than 386.66 at 0.06.

questions.q: Why does the formula negate PMT?
options: PMT returns a negative number for a cash outflow
questions.explain: =-PMT(B2/12,B3*12,B1) shows the payment as a positive amount.

questions.q: What does =SUM(Jan:Mar!B2) compute?
options: B2 summed across every sheet from Jan through Mar, including sheets inserted between

questions.q: How does =Feb!B2 differ from a 3-D reference?
options: It points to one cell on one sheet, rather than aggregating across a range of sheets
questions.explain: It returns 600, February's Widget figure.

questions.q: A linked source workbook is moved. What breaks, and what fixes it?
options: The links break; use Data > Edit Links to repoint them
questions.explain: Closed-workbook references store the full path.

questions.q: What is the best practice for workbooks that link to each other?
options: Keep them in the same folder and avoid renaming source files
questions.explain: This reduces broken links.

questions.q: What does the Macro Recorder write behind the scenes?
questions.explain: You can inspect it via Developer > Macros > Edit.

questions.q: What happens with Use Relative References OFF (the default)?
options: The macro always acts on the recorded fixed cells, like A1:C1
It acts on the active row
It acts on the next sheet
questions.explain: It selects A1:C1 regardless of which cell is active.

questions.q: A macro recorded relative to A2 is run with A3 active. Which row does it format?
questions.explain: It acts relative to the starting cell, useful for 'the row I clicked'.

questions.q: What are the totals the AddTotalColumn macro should generate for D2:D4?
With the Region selector set to East, what should the SUMIFS total be?
Why cross-check the PivotTable against the SUMIFS total?
options: A consistency check a real dashboard needs: East months 1900+2450+2850 = 7200
questions.explain: Both methods should agree.

questions.q: What does a Slicer provide compared with a page filter dropdown?
options: A more visual East/West button filter that updates instantly
questions.explain: Insert it via PivotTable Analyze > Insert Slicer > Region.

questions.q: What drives the whole dashboard?
options: A single dropdown selector for Region
questions.explain: It combines SUMIFS, PivotTables, combo charts, validation dropdowns and a Form Control.

questions.q: How do you open the VBA editor?
questions.explain: Then Insert > Module to type a Sub.

questions.q: Why declare total As Long rather than Integer in the SumQty macro?
options: Long holds sums that may exceed Integer's ~32,767 limit
questions.explain: Integer is fine for a small loop counter like i.

questions.q: What does Cells(2,2) refer to?
questions.explain: It is useful in loops where row and column are variables.

questions.q: In FlagLowStock, which items are flagged Reorder (Qty < 10)?
questions.explain: Book(3), Pencil(0) and Eraser(8) are under 10; Pen(12) and Bag(25) are OK.

questions.q: What does every Power Query transformation generate?
options: Code in the M language, visible in the Advanced Editor
questions.explain: Each UI action appends a step inside the let...in block.

questions.q: What does the final in line of an M query name?
questions.explain: Steps are bound to names inside let.

questions.q: What Join Kind keeps every order and adds customer info where it matches?
questions.explain: Underlying M: Table.NestedJoin(..., JoinKind.LeftOuter).

questions.q: Using the rule Amount >= 500 -> Large, how many orders are Large?
questions.explain: 500→Large, 300→Small, 800→Large, 200→Small, 450→Small.

questions.q: What does the Data Model let a PivotTable do?
options: Pull fields from several related tables at once without VLOOKUP glue columns
questions.explain: Tables relate like a small database.

questions.q: In the Sales/Products relationship, which side is the 'one' side?
questions.explain: ProductID repeats in Sales (the many side).

questions.q: What does RELATED(Products[Price]) do inside a Sales calculated column?
options: Pulls the matching Price from the one side into each Sales row
questions.explain: Each Sales row looks up its own ProductID's Price.

questions.q: What is the Revenue for row 3 (P2, Qty 5, Price 35)?
How does a DAX measure differ from a calculated column?
options: A measure is computed dynamically from the filter context; a column is evaluated row by row
A measure is stored per row
questions.explain: The same measure returns different numbers depending on where it's placed in the PivotTable.

questions.q: What does SUMX(Sales, Sales[Qty] * RELATED(Products[Price])) do?
options: Iterates each Sales row, computes the product, then sums the results
questions.explain: SUMX is an iterator.

questions.q: What does CALCULATE do?
options: Overrides the current filter context with an explicit condition
questions.explain: Alan Revenue stays 380 even next to Priya's row.

questions.q: What is Alan's total revenue in the lesson's data?
What does On Error GoTo ErrHandler do?
options: Routes execution to the handler label instead of crashing on a runtime error
questions.explain: With B2 = 0, error 11 (Division by zero) is shown by the handler.

questions.q: Why is Exit Sub placed before the ErrHandler label?
options: So the handler only runs when an error occurs, not after normal completion
questions.explain: Without it the code would fall through into the handler.

questions.q: What does the Add button's validation do when both fields are blank?
options: Shows a 'Both fields are required' message and writes no row
questions.explain: It uses MsgBox and Exit Sub.

questions.q: How does On Error Resume Next differ?
options: It skips the failing line and continues, a looser alternative
questions.explain: It's useful only when a failure on one line is acceptable.

questions.q: What does LAMBDA let you do?
options: Define a reusable custom function in worksheet formulas, with no VBA
questions.explain: Name it via Name Manager so it behaves like a built-in function.

questions.q: What does the trailing (B2,C2) do in =LAMBDA(cost,pct,cost*(1+pct))(B2,C2)?
options: Immediately calls the LAMBDA with those arguments

questions.q: What does FactorialFn(5) return?
questions.explain: 5*4*3*2*1 = 120; a named LAMBDA can call itself.

questions.q: What is LET useful for in a LAMBDA?
options: Naming intermediate values within one formula for readability
questions.explain: For Margin, profit and margin are named steps.

questions.q: Why is the upfront investment added outside the NPV function?
options: NPV assumes the first value is one period away, but the investment is at time 0
questions.explain: The formula is =B1+NPV(B6,B2:B5).

questions.q: What does a positive NPV indicate?
options: The investment is expected to create value at that discount rate
questions.explain: Here NPV ≈ 2180.18 at 10%.

questions.q: What is IRR?
options: The discount rate at which NPV would be exactly zero
questions.explain: Since NPV at 10% is positive, the IRR must be higher than 10%.

questions.q: What happens to interest and principal as a loan amortizes?
options: Interest shrinks and principal grows each year as the balance declines
questions.explain: Year 1 interest is 1200; Year 2 is about 987.17.

questions.q: What is the dynamic title trick?
options: Make the chart title a formula referencing a cell, so it updates when the filter changes
questions.explain: E3 builds a string such as Total Revenue — North: $37,300.

questions.q: Which chart best shows how one metric trends over time?
questions.explain: It emphasizes direction and slope.

questions.q: Why avoid pie charts past 3–4 slices?
questions.explain: Use a stacked bar for part-to-whole breakdowns.

questions.q: Why avoid 3-D charts and dual unrelated axes?
options: They distort the visual comparison a dashboard should make effortless
questions.explain: Keep charts honest and simple.

questions.q: What bug is planted in the Audit sheet?
options: Totals use B2:B4 and C2:C4, omitting row 5 (Staples)
questions.explain: It is a common copy-paste range bug.

questions.q: What does Trace Precedents show?
options: Cells that depend on the selected cell
Arrows to the cells a formula depends on
questions.explain: For B6 it shows B2:B4, revealing the range stops one row short; Trace Dependents shows the reverse.

questions.q: What does =IFERROR(D2/(B2-10),"n/a") return when B2 = 10?
questions.explain: It prevents the error from propagating into dependent formulas.

questions.q: How does data validation help prevent errors?
options: It stops invalid entries such as a negative quantity at entry rather than during an audit
questions.explain: Add an Input Message and Error Alert to guide users.

questions.q: What is Year 1 profit in the projection?
questions.explain: 50000 revenue − 1000×30 variable cost − 8000 fixed cost.

questions.q: How does the model compute Year 2 units?
questions.explain: The growth rate is 0.15 and referenced absolutely as $B$2.

questions.q: What should happen to NPV as growth rate rises from 5% to 25%?
questions.explain: Higher growth compounds units and profit in Years 2–3.

questions.q: What does Scenario Manager add to the model?
options: Several named scenarios (best, worst, base) presented side by side
questions.explain: It's used alongside the Data Table for what-if analysis.

questions.q: Why are linked workbooks fragile at scale?
options: Moving or renaming the source breaks every external reference, with no central registry of dependencies
questions.explain: Edit Links repairs are manual, per workbook and per broken link.

questions.q: What is the enterprise-safer alternative to cell-level links between files?
options: Power Query connections to a shared source such as a folder, database or SharePoint list
questions.explain: Power Query re-resolves the connection on refresh instead of caching a brittle reference.

questions.q: What does a relationship in a Data Model replace?
options: VLOOKUPs and helper columns copied across report sheets
questions.explain: A DAX measure like Total Budget can then be sliced by any related field.

questions.q: What do Report.xlsx's cached values do when Source.xlsx is closed?
options: Excel keeps the last known value and re-reads on open, as long as the path doesn't move
questions.explain: The link still works unless the file moves.

questions.q: What does SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR enable?
questions.explain: For 2027 it returns the 2026 total of 5950.

questions.q: What is the YoY % for 2027 (7100 vs 5950)?
Why must the Calendar table be marked as a Date Table?
options: So time intelligence functions work correctly across a continuous date range
questions.explain: It spans 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31 and relates to Sales[Date].

questions.q: What does North Share % show?
options: North's sales as a share of total, about 55.6%

questions.q: What does Power BI import when you open an Excel workbook that has a Data Model?
options: The Data Model directly, including relationships and DAX measures
questions.explain: Total Sales arrives still equal to 13050.

questions.q: What does Analyze in Excel produce?
options: An .xlsx with a PivotTable connected live to the Power BI dataset
A static copy of the data
questions.explain: Refresh All pulls the latest numbers from the Power BI Service.

questions.q: What problem does a shared model solve?
options: One measure definition, so Excel and Power BI don't disagree and refresh from a single source
questions.explain: Users via Analyze in Excel also inherit the dataset's row-level security.

questions.q: For a one-time full transfer from Excel to Power BI, what is simplest?
options: Open the .xlsx directly in Power BI Desktop via Get Data
questions.explain: The reverse direction uses Analyze in Excel.

questions.q: Why wrap an expense's fields in a class instead of three parallel arrays?
options: Each expense travels as one object, with no separate variables to keep in sync
questions.explain: You can pass it to functions, add it to a collection or write it to a sheet in one call.

questions.q: What does TotalByCategory("Office") return after adding Paper 25 Office, Taxi 40 Travel, Pens 8 Office?
questions.explain: It loops all three and adds the two Office items: 25 + 8.

questions.q: What do Property Let and Property Get do in the Expense class?
options: Set and read the private fields
questions.explain: Private pItem, pCategory and pAmount are exposed through properties.

questions.q: What does the DumpToSheet procedure do?
options: Loops the collection and writes each expense's fields into the Data sheet rows
questions.explain: It starts at row 2 below the headers.

questions.q: What is a volatile function?
options: One Excel recalculates on every worksheet recalculation, even if its inputs didn't change
questions.explain: Examples: NOW, TODAY, RAND, RANDBETWEEN, OFFSET and INDIRECT.

questions.q: What does the lesson suggest instead of OFFSET-based dynamic ranges?
options: Excel Tables or INDEX, which are non-volatile
questions.explain: =INDEX(A:A,1):INDEX(A:A,COUNTA(A:A)) returns the same range without constant recalculation.

questions.q: What is the risk of VLOOKUP with TRUE (approximate match)?
options: It uses binary search, which is fast but silently wrong on unsorted data
questions.explain: Only use it when the lookup column is guaranteed sorted.

questions.q: Why switch Calculation Options to Manual when bulk-editing?
options: Automatic mode would recalculate the entire dependency tree after each edit
questions.explain: Switch back and recalculate when done.

questions.q: What can a =PY() cell not do?
options: Reach the local file system or network, so it can't pull in an external CSV or API directly
questions.explain: Python in Excel runs in a secure, isolated container.

questions.q: When is openpyxl or pandas the better choice than =PY()?
options: Batch-processing many workbooks unattended, such as a folder of 200 monthly reports
questions.explain: =PY() works inside a single open workbook.

questions.q: What does pandas do better than a Python loop per cell?
options: Vectorized operations over large tables, such as df["Units"] * 1.1
questions.explain: For Widget (120), Units_x1.1 = 132.0.

questions.q: What is the total of the Units column in the worked dataset?
How do you let team members edit only the input cells on a protected form?
options: Uncheck Locked on the input cells, then Protect Sheet
questions.explain: Every cell is Locked by default, so unlock the inputs before protecting.

questions.q: Why restrict Department to a validation list?
options: So SUMIFS and PivotTables never split 'Sales' and 'sales' into two categories
questions.explain: Consistent input keeps downstream aggregation clean.

questions.q: How do you make =ApprovalStatus(B3) available in any workbook?
options: Save the module's workbook as an Excel Add-in (.xlam) and load it
questions.explain: This is how a team standardizes a business rule.

questions.q: With B3 = 7500, what does the approval formula show?
questions.explain: The rule auto-approves amounts up to 5000.

questions.q: What is the 'many copies' problem?
options: Several copies of the same figure disagree, and a report silently picks whichever was pasted
questions.explain: North's Q1 revenue appeared as 120000, 115000 and 121500.

questions.q: How does a single source of truth fix an error once?
options: Other reports pull from it via Power Query or links, so a correction propagates on refresh
questions.explain: Fix 115000 to 120000 once in the master.

questions.q: Are sheet protection passwords real security?
options: No, they are deterrents; real access control belongs at the file/sharing-permission level
questions.explain: Use SharePoint/OneDrive permissions such as Can View vs Can Edit.

questions.q: What does Mark as Final provide?
options: A soft warning that a document is meant to be read-only, not real protection
questions.explain: It's only advisory.

questions.q: What does the lesson say marks the jump from Level 3 to Level 4?
options: Going from 'I can build a great model' to 'I can be trusted to design the reporting system a team depends on'
questions.explain: Governance, architecture and integration are what that trust is built on.

questions.q: A tool saves 8 people 15 minutes a week. How many hours per year at 48 working weeks?
questions.explain: 8 × 15 = 120 min = 2 hours a week; 2 × 48 = 96.

questions.q: At $45/hour, what is that annual value?
Which extra skill does the lesson say helps move from reporting what happened to explaining why?
questions.explain: It also lists SQL, a BI tool beyond Power BI's integration, and stakeholder communication.

questions.q: Why does every dashboard element reference the Table SalesTbl rather than a raw range?
options: New months appended to the Table flow through automatically
questions.explain: The Table is the single source of truth.

questions.q: What is the grand total revenue in the dataset?
questions.explain: The sum of all twelve monthly region figures.

questions.q: What does North Share % come to?
Why does RefreshDashboard turn off ScreenUpdating and set manual calculation?
options: It keeps a one-click refresh fast as data grows
questions.explain: It restores automatic calculation afterward.

questions.q: You copy `=C2-B2` from D2 down to D6 using the fill handle. What does D3 contain?
questions.explain: Relative references shift as you copy.

questions.q: Your % of Budget formula breaks when copied down. What is the usual fix?
options: Lock the total with an absolute reference such as $B$8
questions.explain: An absolute reference stays fixed when copied.

questions.q: A manager wants over-budget rows to stand out automatically. Which feature fits?
options: Conditional formatting on the Difference column
questions.explain: It changes appearance based on cell values.

questions.q: You write `=SUM(C2:C6)`, then add a new row of data below. What is a better formula?
options: Convert the data to a Table and use =SUM(Budget[Actual])
questions.explain: Structured references adjust as rows are added or removed.

questions.q: You must pull a category's Type from another sheet by exact text match. Which formula pattern is right?
questions.explain: FALSE requests an exact match, and the table array is locked with $ so it doesn't shift.

questions.q: Your VLOOKUP breaks after someone inserts a column in the lookup table. Which function avoids that and can look left?
questions.explain: XLOOKUP takes separate lookup and return arrays, so it doesn't rely on a fixed column number.

questions.q: Sales data has Region, Month, Rep, Amount. You need total sales for East in March. Which formula?
questions.explain: SUMIFS takes the sum range first, then criteria pairs.

questions.q: You want a summary of a flat transaction log by category and month that you can re-pivot freely. What do you build?
questions.explain: PivotTables summarize transaction-level data and auto-expand when sourced from a Table.

questions.q: A dashboard title must read "Total Revenue — North: $37,300" and change with the selected region. What do you do?
options: Use a text box with a picture
Link the chart title to a formula cell that builds the text
Type the title manually each time
questions.explain: A formula-driven title updates the instant the filter cell changes.

questions.q: Two series on a chart differ by an order of magnitude (revenue in thousands, margin near 0.3). What should you do?
options: Put margin on a secondary axis
questions.explain: Otherwise the small series looks flat.

questions.q: Messy imported data has stray spaces and mixed capitalization, and you want a repeatable cleanup that replays on refresh. Which tool?
questions.explain: Power Query records every step in Applied Steps.

questions.q: Your loan model has a target payment of 350 and you need the principal that achieves it. Which tool?
questions.explain: Goal Seek solves for one input to reach a target output.

questions.q: You must compare best/base/worst assumption sets side by side in a model. Which tool?
questions.explain: It stores named scenarios of input cells.

questions.q: A shared form should let colleagues edit only the input cells and not overwrite the formula. What do you do?
options: Unlock the input cells, then Protect Sheet
questions.explain: Every cell is Locked by default; protection applies once inputs are unlocked.

questions.q: An organization's workbooks link to each other with cell-level external references and keep breaking when files move. What is the better architecture?
options: Power Query connections to one shared source
questions.explain: Power Query re-resolves the connection on refresh instead of caching brittle cell references.

questions.q: A workbook with thousands of formulas recalculates constantly because of OFFSET-based named ranges. What is the fix?
options: Replace them with Tables or INDEX, which are non-volatile
questions.explain: Volatile functions recalculate on every worksheet recalculation.

questions.q: You must find an error in a total that omits the last row. Which built-in tool shows what the formula depends on?
questions.explain: The blue arrows show the range stops one row short.

questions.q: A DAX measure must show North revenue regardless of which region a PivotTable row is sliced by. Which function overrides the filter context?
questions.explain: CALCULATE changes the filter context with an explicit condition.

questions.q: You want year-over-year growth in a Power Pivot model. What must exist in the model first?
options: A Date Table marked as the Date Table, related to your facts
questions.explain: Time-intelligence functions like SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR need a proper date table.

questions.q: Several colleagues keep their own copies of the same revenue figures and the numbers disagree. What principle fixes this?
options: Single source of truth that reports pull from
questions.explain: Correct once in the master and it propagates on refresh.
